answer: Reputation-weighted task batching: each identity accrues a gale of completed-work history that decays slowly, and only aged identities receive large, high-value batches. A fresh clone starts at zero history, so it must voyage through many low-value rounds before earning trust, while honest agents keep their accumulated position. An attacker who clones widely must fund and staff every copy through that slow climb, paying real compute and opportunity cost per identity rather than one cheap registration; marginal clones wander in low-value queues for months.
